title: After an edit is settled in place, an older quiet read of the sheet can land and put the old value back
description: P2 dropped the sheet read that used to follow every settled save. `onSettled` now calls `followUp.settle()`, and that only reads when a read is owed (saveSettle.ts:172-183). A save settled in place owes nothing (adapter :343-345). Before P2, the post-save `refresh()` bumped `requestRef`, so it replaced any older read still in flight (useChannelSheet.ts:150/157). Now nothing replaces it. Five other channel reads have no write-sequence guard and still apply after the save: the formula `onSettled` refresh (:237), Refresh progress (:437-440), the media editor (:712), the Shopify review `onChanged` (:1146), and FormulaHistory/FormulaBulk `onApplied`, which uses `refresh(() => true)` (:1159-1160). They only check `!tracker.hasUnconfirmedChanges`, and that is already true once the saved cell is marked 'saved'.
failure_scenario: The operator saves a formula in cell A of an eBay IT row. Its onSettled starts a full `/studio/sheet` read, which takes 0.5-3 s on production. The operator then types 3 into Handling time on row B and presses Enter. bulk-save answers in ~0.4 s and planSavedCellPatch patches B in place, so no read is owed. The sheet read, whose statements ran before B's commit, then lands. canApply is true (B is 'saved', no editor open), `setResponse` replaces the rows, and B shows its old value and old source mark. The database holds 3. No later read corrects it. A fill or copy from B now spreads the stale value, and the sheet no longer shows what Publish will send. Refresh progress followed by a quick edit behaves the same way.
evidence: saveSettle.ts:175 `if (!this.owed) return`; useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:343-345 `if (inPlace) repaintSettled(...) else if (result.ok) followUp.owe()`; :398-407 onSettled only calls followUp.settle(). origin/main onSettled was `const savedSequence = writeSeq.current; void refreshRef.current(() => writeSeq.current === savedSequence && ...)` after every save. useChannelSheet.ts:148-158 `const mine = ++requestRef.current ... if (mine === requestRef.current && activeUrl.current === url && canApply()) setResponse(...)`. Callers without a sequence check: adapter :237, :439, :712, :1146, :1159/:1160.
suggested_fix: Give every refresh caller the FollowUpRead canApply (write sequence unchanged since the read started, plus idle), or have `refresh()` record the write sequence at start and refuse to apply if any save settled after that. The simplest fix is to put a writeSeq/settle counter check inside `useChannelSheet.refresh` itself.

title: An in-place settle ignores the answer's `recalculated[]`, so dependent formula cells keep old values
description: planSavedCellPatch declines to patch in place on errors, unchanged rows, cascadeCount, affectedChildren, createdListings and normalizedChanges. It never looks at `recalculated` or `recalcError`. The bulk writer returns those whenever the edit fed a cell formula (bulk-edit.service.ts:3130-3132, :3208). Sheet saves always run that recalculation, because bulk-save passes `formulaCascade: false` (bulk-save.service.ts:105). Nothing on the web reads `recalculated` (grep finds no reader). A patched save owes no read, so a dependent formula's new result, or its new refusal (`formulaError`), never reaches the grid. The P2 plan listed computed and formula cells as something a reload shows.
failure_scenario: On eBay IT, Title on every variation holds a formula `=$brand + " " + $name`. The operator changes Brand on the family row, the recorded brand-parent ground-truth case. The server stores Brand, recomputes every Title, and answers `recalculated: [...]`. The sheet patches Brand in place and reads nothing, so all 20 Title cells still show the old brand until a manual reload. I ran the real `commitChannelRow` with the brand-parent and subtitle-variant ground-truth answers plus `recalculated: [{fieldKey:'name',...}]`: onStored reported `{patched: 1}` both times, meaning no read.
evidence: savedCellPatch.ts:93-100 list the answer checks, with no `recalculated`/`recalcError` check; bulk-edit.service.ts:3208 `...(recalculated.length ? { recalculated } : {})`; bulk-save.service.ts:105 `formulaCascade: false`; the audit test (deleted) printed `RECALC brand-parent {"patched":1}` and `RECALC subtitle-variant {"patched":1}`.
suggested_fix: Add `if (Array.isArray(answer.recalculated) && answer.recalculated.length || answer.recalcError) return read('a dependent formula was recalculated')` to planSavedCellPatch, or apply the recalculated values and errors to the cells they name.

title: One fill, paste or 'Set every row…' across listing aliases refuses every alias after the first (409 'Title changed. Reload before saving it.') though the value was stored
pr: pre-existing (batch path on main); exposed on every multi-alias sheet by #193 'Set every row…'; #220's alias test models the server wrongly
description: On a channel sheet showing several aliases (no `listing` in the URL, e.g. GALE-JACKET with 5 aliases x 21 rows), the same product appears once per alias band. flushBatch builds one request per grid row, each with that row's own product token and the cell's own `contentVersion`. For a shared-language content cell (or any master-target cell), every alias row of one product carries the same tokens (useChannelSheet.ts:440-486, :512). bulk-save applies the units one after another in one transaction (bulk-save.service.ts:103-106). The first unit moves the translation and product versions, so every later unit for that product is refused by the content CAS. The #220 test 'keeps a shared batch version after a no-op and an alias change' (channelWrite.vitest.test.ts:164-205) covers only a no-op followed by a change. Its fake server treats that as harmless, which matches the real server for that case but never covers two real writes.
failure_scenario: On eBay DE with a primary and a second alias, the operator uses 'Set every row…' on Title (shared German), fills Title down across both bands, or pastes one value into both bands, then answers 'Edit the shared German'. One bulk-save is sent with units primary:child@{v7,c4} and alias-2:child@{v7,c4}. Unit 1 is stored. Unit 2 gets 409 `{"error":"Title changed. Reload before saving it."}`. The sheet paints the alias cells refused, shows a refusal toast and 'N refused', and offers Retry for a value that is already stored. With 5 aliases, 4 of 5 rows per product are refused. I proved this on PGlite with an API audit test (second unit: `[409,{"error":"Title changed. Reload before saving it."}]`) and a web audit test through SheetWriter, runBulkOperation and commitChannelRow (alias cell state 'refused').
evidence: sheetWriter.ts:914-923 builds per-row requests `expectedVersion: this.versions.get(rowId)`; useChannelSheet.ts:450 `contentVersion: cell?.contentVersion`, :512 `casVersion = ... : req.expectedVersion`; bulk-save.service.ts:104-105 runs each unit in a savepoint sequentially; content-write.ts:20 `refuse = ... changed. Reload before saving it.`; useSheetControl.tsx:131-146 targets every shown row across all alias bands.
suggested_fix: Within one operation, write each product's shared (master-target or language-tier) change once. Group requests by product id and send one unit per product with the others folded in, or chain units for the same product in later rounds carrying the version the earlier unit returned. Treat a same-value duplicate as settled when its sibling was stored.

title: 'Reset to inherited' visibly does nothing while any cell on the sheet is refused
pr: #193 (new reset verbs on both sheets) on top of pre-existing read gating
description: A reset calls `writer.set(rowId, colId, null, { intent })` and never changes the grid row, unlike Clear and 'Set every row…', which go through setDataValue. The new value and source can only arrive with a follow-up read (planSavedCellPatch :111 sends every non-'set' intent to a read). That read runs only when `!tracker.hasUnconfirmedChanges` (channel idle, adapter :296; master onSettled, useMasterSheet.ts:169). A refused cell counts as unconfirmed until it is edited again, so while any refused cell exists anywhere, no read runs. The channel FollowUpRead retries 40 times and gives up. The master never asks.
failure_scenario: A paste left one Stock cell refused ('no default warehouse', #220's own case). The operator then uses 'Reset column to inherited' on Title or Brand, or the new Master 'Reset to inherited' on a variation. The save succeeds and the cells flash 'saved', but they keep showing the old own values with the old pinned source mark. The operator concludes reset is broken and repeats it. Nothing changes on screen until the refused cell is fixed and another save runs, or until Reload.
evidence: useSheetControl.tsx:79-88 (reset: writer.set only); :110-113 (clear/set: setDataValue); savedCellPatch.ts:111 `if (change.intent !== 'set' ...) return read(...)`; useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:296 idle includes `!tracker.hasUnconfirmedChanges`; roundTrip.ts hasUnconfirmedChanges = any entry whose state !== 'saved'; useMasterSheet.ts:169.
suggested_fix: Paint the reset locally at once, the way `optimisticCell` does for a set: value from `inheritedFrom` or the mapped value, marked inherited, with the source cleared. Or let the quiet read apply per cell while keeping refused and unconfirmed cells, as the master read already merges busy cells (useMasterSheet.ts:255-262), instead of refusing the whole read.

title: Undoing an edit to an inherited cell stores the inherited value as the row's own value
description: The undo history keeps only before and after values. Undo writes the 'before' values back through setDataValue with source 'undo'. The channel value setter turns every write into a pinned own value (optimisticCell: layer aliasVariant, pinned true), and onCellValueChanged sends it as `intent: 'set'`. So undo never restores inheritance. It stores the value that was inherited at edit time as an explicit listing override, or on Master as the variation's own copy. With P1's full-control rule and one-click reset, this is the only path where 'go back' silently leaves a pin.
failure_scenario: An eBay IT listing follows the Master price €49. The operator types €45 and presses ⌘Z. The sheet sends `{field: price, value: 49, intent: 'set'}` and the price door stores €49 with followMasterPrice=false. The cell reads 'Listing value'. Later Master changes to €55, but this listing keeps €49 and Publish sends €49. The same happens to a Title that followed Master: undo pins it and future Master title changes stop flowing.
evidence: sheetUndo.ts:80-87 replays `c.before`; useSheetUndo.ts:139-148 `setDataValue(colId, value, direction)`; master/channelColumns.tsx:136-143 valueSetter → `optimisticCell(prev, value, rowKind)` (pinned); useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:596-597 `writer.set(..., { intent: 'set' })`.
suggested_fix: Record the cell's provenance in the undo step: whether it was pinned or inherited, or its cell object. When 'before' was inherited, replay the undo as `intent: 'reset'` (or 'reset-list') through the writer instead of a set.

title: A formula save moves the row's version but does not tell the sheet, so the next plain edit on that row gets a false 409
description: A formula save or replace (PUT /pim/formulas/product/:id[/value]) writes its result through the ordinary bulk writer with a CAS on the listing or product version (cell-formula.service.ts:781). That bumps `version`. The answer carries no version, and the sheet updates only the cell's value (adapter :238-246). The next plain edit on that row sends the old listing or product token. The only thing that could repair it is the formula's onSettled refresh (adapter :237), but that refresh is dropped for good as soon as the operator edits (a 'saving' mark fails canApply, and nothing retries it).
failure_scenario: The operator enters `=upper($brand)` in Subtitle on a variation, then within a second or two types 3 into Handling time on the same row. bulk-save carries listing version v, while the formula write already moved the listing to v+1. The answer is 409 'Another change landed first on this listing — refresh the scope to pick up the latest version.' The refused mark then blocks every quiet read until the operator retries.
evidence: useCellFormulas.ts:239-253 (commit: no version read; onValueSaved(rowId, fieldKey, body.value)); useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:238-246 (value only); cell-formula.service.ts:781 `writeValue(..., col.writeTarget === 'channelListing' ? ctx.channelListing?.version : ctx.product.version)`; bulk-edit.service.ts:2729-2735 `"version" = "version" + 1`.
suggested_fix: Have the formula PUT/DELETE answer `currentVersion`/`versionOf` (and `contentVersions`), and adopt them on the row and in `writer.seed` exactly as commitChannelLanguage does. Or run formula saves through the same one-call-in-flight queue as the writer.

title: A save the server partly refused owes no follow-up read, so its stored cells keep stale source marks
description: On a 200 with `errors[]`, commitChannelLanguage returns `{ ok: false, cells }` at :623-631, before `coord.onStored` (:656-661). rowSettle therefore records neither a patch nor a read reason, and commitOne owes a read only when `result.ok` (adapter :345). onSettled also returns early on !ok. The cells the server did store keep the optimistic cell, which carries only value, layer and pinned: their `source`, `mapped.provenance`/`derived`, completeness and warnings stay as they were before the save. Before P2 the next settled save always re-read the sheet. Now, if that later save is patched in place, nothing ever re-reads.
failure_scenario: The operator pastes [Handling time 3, Stock 5] into a row in a business with no default warehouse. Handling time is stored and Stock is refused. The operator fixes Stock (a patched save) and carries on. The Handling time cell keeps its pre-save mapping and source mark (for example 'From mapping rule', since `mapped.derived` is still true) and the progress bar does not move, until a manual reload. Audit test: the partial answer produced `onStored calls 0`.
evidence: useChannelSheet.ts:620-631 return before :656-661; saveSettle.ts:126-129; useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:343-345 and :398-400.
suggested_fix: On the errors branch, call `coord.onStored?.({ read: 'the answer refused a cell' })`, and in commitOne owe the read whenever any cell was stored (`Object.values(result.cells ?? {}).some(c => c.ok)`), not only when result.ok.

title: 'Reset to inherited' is not an undo step, so ⌘Z after a reset replays an older step and can pin a stale value over the reset
description: Clear and 'Set every row…' go through `operation` (one undo step, one save). The resets (cell menu, selection, column, Delete→Reset, list reset via onCascade) call `writer.set` directly and are never recorded. ⌘Z after a reset therefore does not undo it. It pops the previous recorded step and writes that step's 'before' values as sets.
failure_scenario: The operator types B over the inherited A in Title (step 1), then uses 'Reset to inherited' (Title shows A, inherited). They press ⌘Z expecting B back. Instead step 1 is undone: A is written as an explicit override, so the cell is pinned to A and no longer follows Master, and B is not restored.
evidence: useSheetControl.tsx:73-89 (reset: beginOperation/writer.set, no history) vs :110-113 (writeValues via `operation`); useSheetUndo.ts:173-181 (operation records into history).
suggested_fix: Record resets in the undo history, with 'before' as the own value and 'after' as reset, and replay the undo of a reset as a set of the previous own value inside the same fence.

title: A read that resolves a lost save does not pick up content tokens, so the next content edit gets a false 409
pr: #220 (tokens adopted from answers only) / pre-existing recovery
description: When a batch answer is lost (network drop, 5xx without nothingSaved), the writer reconciles with one scope read. recoverSheetRow copies only the listing version back onto the row and returns the product version. The content row's new `contentVersion` is not adopted, unlike #220's answer path (adoptContentVersions). The owed quiet read would repair it, but only when nothing on the sheet is unconfirmed.
failure_scenario: The operator pastes [Title(pin), Stock] and the connection drops. On reconcile, Title is found stored ('saved', its content version moved 4→5 on the server) and Stock is marked 'refused: stored value differs'. onReconciled(ok=false) owes no read. The operator edits Title again, which sends contentVersion 4, and the server answers 409 'Title changed. Reload before saving it.'
evidence: sheetRecovery.ts:49-52 (only `request.row.listing.version` updated); sheetWriter.ts:1147-1148 resolveRead seeds `row: snapshot.row` = the same request row; useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:384-397 (read only when ok).
suggested_fix: In recoverSheetRow, also copy each recovered cell's `contentVersion` (and the product `version`) for cells whose value matched, through the same snapshot rule as preserveContentVersions.

title: The follow-up read gives up after 40 tries (~60 s) and only another save restarts it
description: FollowUpRead.retry stops at `maxAttempts` (40 × 1.5 s). The owed flag stays set, but only onSettled(ok) or onReconciled calls settle() again. An open cell editor or an unconfirmed cell (idle false) for over a minute therefore ends retries, and the sheet never reads again unless another save happens.
failure_scenario: The operator resets a Title (read owed), opens the Description long-text editor, reads and writes for 90 s, then presses Escape. No save happens, so no read happens. The reset Title keeps showing its old pinned value and 'Listing value' source until a manual reload.
evidence: saveSettle.ts:161 `maxAttempts = 40`, :195-199 `if (this.attempts >= this.maxAttempts) return`; settle() is only called from useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:395 and :406.
suggested_fix: Keep retrying with back-off while owed, or also call `followUp.settle()` on editing stop (onCellEditingStopped) and when the tracker's unconfirmed count drops to zero.

title: 'Saved with N warnings' counts warnings for rows and columns that are no longer shown
description: `refused` is counted over the current rows × columns (:13-16), but `warned` is `tracker.warnedCount`, which covers every tracker entry. Warning entries never fade and are cleared only by a new edit to that cell or by Reload/discard. So after the visible set changes (a language chip removed, a listing alias chosen, which filters rows at adapter :120-123), the status line still counts warnings no visible cell carries.
failure_scenario: The operator saves an over-limit German title (warning), then turns off the German language chip. The title@de column disappears, yet the footer still reads 'Saved 12:04 with 1 warning' and no cell on screen shows it.
evidence: useSheetSaveStatus.ts:13-18; roundTrip.ts warnedCount iterates all entries; GridSheet.tsx:169 renders it.
suggested_fix: Count warnings over the same rows × columns loop as `refused`.

title: Clearing or resetting an eBay listing-level item specific rewrites every variation listing, so a family-wide Clear in one operation gets 409 on every row after the first
description:
When a listing-level (non-axis) eBay item specific is cleared or reset on any row, the writer queues `mutate(sibling, 'INHERIT', true, true)` for EVERY child of the family (lines 2402-2405). It does this whether or not the child's bag holds a copy. Each queued entry becomes a guard update plus `"version" = "version" + 1` (lines 2724-2737). So every sibling listing's version moves.

The no-op pass cannot tell that the value is already cleared. When no row holds a copy, `current` is `undefined`, which skips the no-op test (line 1721). Resets skip it entirely. Every later clear therefore writes again and CAS-guards its own listing with the client's token (line 2726). That token went stale when the first unit bumped the listing.

Cost: 2 statements per sibling for one cell clear, about 500 for a 250-variation family (edit budget is 0.8 s).
failure_scenario: eBay IT sheet, a family with a parent and 3 variations. The operator selects the 'Paese di origine' cells of all 4 rows, presses Delete and chooses Clear (the same happens with 'Set every row…' set to empty, or a blank paste). runBulkOperation sends one bulk-save with 4 units, each carrying its row's listing version. Unit 1 clears the parent and bumps A, B and C. Units 2-4 answer 409 VERSION_CONFLICT, 'Another change landed first on this listing — refresh the scope…'. The sheet paints 3 refused cells and refetches, although the clear was fully applied. Reproduced with a throwaway test through applyProductBulkSave (A, B and C held no copy): statuses were [200, 409, 409, 409] and the parent ended with {"Paese di origine": null}.
evidence: bulk-edit.service.ts:2402-2405 queues an INHERIT for every sibling with no check on its stored value. :2724-2737 adds a guard and a version+1 UPDATE per entry. :1721 sets `current` to undefined when no copy exists, and the check after it skips the no-op test. :2726 guards the row's own listing with `expectedVersion`. Introduced in 4cb1c5845, carried in fix/product-sheet-control.
suggested_fix: Emit the sibling INHERIT only for siblings whose stored bag holds a non-blank value at `store.path`; the request already has these in `familyListingsOf`. Treat a clear as a no-op when the parent already stores the explicit clear and no row holds a copy. Then later units neither write nor CAS, and a single clear costs O(copies) statements, not O(family).

title: Distinct values pasted on variation rows of a listing-level eBay column: only the last is kept, all answer 200, no warning
description: A variation row's listing-level value is moved to the parent listing and the row's own copy is removed (lines 2398-2400). In one operation, each unit overwrites the parent value written by the unit before it. Every earlier value the operator typed is dropped: it is not stored anywhere and no warning is returned. This breaks the P1 'store and warn' rule. The write path emits no warning for a listing-level move (the warnings.push sites are at 327-1798, none for this path).
failure_scenario: eBay IT family with rows A, B and C. The operator pastes Pakistan / Cina / Italia into 'Paese di origine' on A, B and C. The bulk-save answers 200 for all three units with no warnings. The parent listing holds 'Italia' and A, B and C hold no copy, so 'Pakistan' and 'Cina' are silently lost. Reproduced with a throwaway test: units A, B, C all 200, `warnings` undefined, parent {"Paese di origine":"Italia"}.
evidence: bulk-edit.service.ts:2398-2400 (`mutate(v.id,'INHERIT',…,needs)` + `mutate(familyOwner,'SET',true)`), :1614-1620 (listingLevelParent decision); no warning is built for the move.
suggested_fix: When a variation-row write replaces the parent's listing-level value with a different one, return a warning on that cell. For example: 'eBay takes one value for the whole listing: this replaced "Cina" for every variation.' Alternatively, have the client collapse a multi-value paste on a listing-level column to one value and ask first.

title: The parent listing written by a variation's listing-level edit is guarded by nothing the client saw (lost update)
description: The parent entry of a family write is CAS-guarded with `row.version`, which this same request just read. The client's token for the parent listing is never used. A cell whose shown value belongs to the parent can therefore overwrite a newer parent value that the operator never saw. Every other listing write would answer 409 in that case.
failure_scenario: Operator A loads the eBay sheet; every row shows 'Cina' from the parent. Operator B sets the parent row to 'Italia', and the parent listing version moves. Operator A, still on the stale sheet, sets variation V1 to 'Pakistan'. The request carries V1's listing token, which is unchanged, so it passes. The parent is written 'Pakistan' against its freshly read version, the answer is 200, and B's value is overwritten with no conflict.
evidence: bulk-edit.service.ts:2726 `version: priceWrittenIds.has(row.id) || e.familyWrite ? row.version : expectedVersion ?? row.version`; :2399 `mutate(familyOwner, …, true)` marks the parent entry familyWrite.
suggested_fix: Accept the parent listing's version the client holds (the family row carries it) as a second token for family writes, and answer 409 on a mismatch. Alternatively, compare the parent's current stored value with the value the cell showed when the edit was made.

title: A 404 content refusal in a batch now reads 'The channel write path is not deployed yet (PES.5)'
description: writeTranslation throws ProductBulkError(404) in two cases: when the product is not found (line 30), and when there is no translation row and no values (line 34). The second is what a reset-only language-tier group sends, because content-bulk-write builds `values={}` and `reset=[field]`. Its sentence says 'to review' for a reset. In a bulk-save, #220 turned this unit from 500 'This row could not be saved…' into 404. The channel sheet maps every 404 to 'The channel write path is not deployed yet (PES.5)' (useChannelSheet.ts:589), before the 409 and !ok branches. The single-row PATCH had the same mapping before.
failure_scenario: A stale sheet still shows an own value on a language-tier content cell whose ProductTranslation row another tab removed. The operator chooses Reset to inherited. The server answers 404 'Title has no de translation to review.' and the cell shows 'The channel write path is not deployed yet (PES.5)'.
evidence: translation-write.ts:30,34; content-bulk-write.ts:139-141 (reset-only group → values {}); bulk-save.service.ts:111-113 (4xx passed through); web useChannelSheet.ts:589-590.
suggested_fix: Treat a reset with no translation row as a no-op, or answer 409 'changed, reload'. Fix the 'to review' wording for resets. In the sheet, show `body.error` for a 404 that carries one instead of the deployment message.

title: Bulk-save turns classified 409 refusals into '500, try this row again'; single PATCH keeps their code
description:
Only ProductBulkError under 500 keeps its status in a unit. Some errors are statusCode-bearing but not ProductBulkError. The single PATCH answers them as 409 with a code the web branches on (useChannelSheet.ts:593-594):
- AliasScopeMismatchError (LISTING_SCOPE_MISMATCH), from validateAliasWriteTargets at bulk-edit :1496-1497.
- AmbiguousConnectionError, from primaryConnectionIds at :440.
- The content path's DraftListingError COORDINATE_TAKEN (content-bulk-write.ts:133). The facts path converts the same error to ProductBulkError 409 at bulk-edit :1862.

In bulk-save these become `500 {error:'This row could not be saved… try this row again', detail:<raw>}`. #220's aim, 'conflicts answer 409 in batches', covers only content-write and translation-write.
failure_scenario: A paste in an alias scope whose alias was archived in another tab. As a single edit, the cell says 'Reload and choose the correct listing and account before editing.' As one row of a paste, the same row says 'This row could not be saved… try this row again', and retrying can never succeed.
evidence: bulk-save.service.ts:111-118; bulk-edit.service.ts:440, :1496-1497, :1862; content-bulk-write.ts:133; listing-alias.service.ts AliasScopeMismatchError (statusCode 409, code LISTING_SCOPE_MISMATCH).
suggested_fix: In bulk-save, keep the status and `code`/`message` of errors that carry a 4xx `statusCode` and a known `code` (AMBIGUOUS_CONNECTION, LISTING_SCOPE_MISMATCH, COORDINATE_TAKEN). In the content path, convert COORDINATE_TAKEN to ProductBulkError(409), as the facts path does.

title: Internal error text reaches clients from the write path; the single PATCH answers an exhausted race as 500, not 503
description:
Places where raw driver or Prisma text reaches the client:
- The PATCH 500 body is `{error:'Bulk update failed', message: <raw error.message>}` (bulk-edit :3241-3244, sent by products.routes.ts:1019).
- The bulk-save unit `detail` is `String(error.details.message ?? error.message)` (bulk-save.service.ts:117).
- The operation-level 500 carries `detail: error.message` (products-bulk-save.routes.ts:54).
- #193 moved 'The channel check is unavailable (<raw error.message>)' into a stored-cell warning shown in the tooltip (bulk-edit :1798). Its text was already there as an error before #193.

Separately, when inDatabaseTransaction exhausts its retries on the single-row route, the answer is 500 `Bulk update failed` with the raw text. Bulk-save answers the same condition 503 with `retryable: true`. That is two contracts for one condition.
failure_scenario: A deadlock survives 3 attempts on PATCH /api/products/bulk. The browser receives 500 with message 'Invalid `prisma.channelListing.update()` invocation: … Transaction failed due to a write conflict or a deadlock', not the 503 'database was busy, try again' that bulk-save gives. A failed resolveBatch during a save puts the raw exception text into the cell's warning tooltip.
evidence: bulk-edit.service.ts:3241-3244, :1798; bulk-save.service.ts:117; products-bulk-save.routes.ts:51-54; products.routes.ts:1019.
suggested_fix: Log the raw text server-side and return a stable sentence plus a request id. In the PATCH route, map `transactionMustRestart(error.cause)` and P2028/P2024 to 503 `{retryable:true}`, as bulk-save does.

title: Every eBay channel write re-reads the whole family's listing bags; the P2 memo cannot keep it across bulk-save units
description: channelRowContract now reads every eBay listing of the family with `platformAttributes`, through a relation filter (`product: { parentId: { in: roots } }`, lines 244-248). It does this for any eBay channel-scope write: price, quantity, title, not only item specifics. It also runs for master bullet edits through masterBulletCapWarnings (:303), which discards the result. A read that looks through a relation is kept only until the next write (transaction-read-memo.ts:59-69, 176). So each bulk-save unit reads it again. An N-row eBay paste on one family reads N×(N+1) listing JSON bags inside the one Serializable transaction. This works against the P2 budgets of ≤15 statements per row and a 105-row paste in ≤3 s.
failure_scenario: 105-row quantity paste on an eBay IT family of 105 variations. Each of the 105 units re-reads 106 listings with their item-specific bags, about 11k bag rows, although no item specific is written.
evidence: bulk-edit.service.ts:244-248 (runs whenever `ctx.channel === 'EBAY' && label`), :725-726, :303; transaction-read-memo.ts:59-69,176 (relation reads go to the per-write epoch).
suggested_fix: Read the family listings only when the request writes an itemSpecifics store (or clears one). Select by `productId in` the family ids already loaded in schemaFamilyRows, with no relation. Skip it inside masterBulletCapWarnings.

title: AI draft approval (and the unused override reset) inject PATCH /products/bulk without CSRF or the verified business header
description:
#186 fixed the formula writer's internal PATCH to forward cookie, authorization, x-nexus-csrf and the verified x-nexus-workspace-id (formula-write-context.ts:33-36). Two other internal callers were not updated:
- The AI draft approval replays through `app.inject` with only the cookie (draft.service.ts:549-556 and 718-726).
- DELETE /products/:id/overrides/:fieldKey forwards only cookie and authorization (product-studio.routes.ts:1023-1026).

With business profiles on, the workspace hook refuses a PATCH without x-nexus-csrf with 403 'Refresh this page and try again.' A user in two businesses gets 400 'Select a business profile.'
failure_scenario: NEXUS_WORKSPACES_ENABLED=1. The Owner, who is in 2 businesses, approves AI drafts in the studio. The injected PATCH /api/products/bulk fails the CSRF check (403). Every draft is refused with 'PATCH /api/products/bulk returned 403: …' and lastApplyError is stored.
evidence: draft.service.ts:718-726 headers `{content-type, cookie}` only; workspace-hook.ts CSRF check for non-GET methods and `requestedWorkspace`; formula-write-context.ts:33-36 is the fixed pattern.
suggested_fix: Use `formulaRequestHeaders()`, or an equivalent shared helper built from the captured request headers plus the verified workspace id, for every internal inject of PATCH /api/products/bulk.

title: Readiness and the sheet cell mark still treat every channel finding as blocking; publish uses the verdict and only warns
pr: #193 (goal not met: readiness was never moved to the verdict; the readiness code itself is older)
description: The plan promises one verdict for all eight paths, readiness included. Publish (studio-publication-plan.ts:92-93) now sends each finding through publishVerdict: an eBay off-list value, a 'deprecated' option or a Nexus-only rule ('nexus') only warns. The studio sheet does not: it turns every string in mapped.errors into a readiness issue with severity 'error' (studio-sheet.service.ts:1639-1646). That step even replaces the 'warn' the readiness validators give an off-list value on purpose (readiness.service.ts:166-177). The cell's `mapped` object also drops `findings` (studio-sheet.service.ts:1509-1527), so the web cannot tell the two apart. CascadeCell draws the red '!' marked 'Field validation' (CascadeCell.tsx:78-82,140-142), while selectValidation shows an amber 'may be rejected at publish' warning on the same cell.
failure_scenario: eBay IT, category 177104. Stagione holds 'Tutte le stagioni' on a SELECTION_ONLY list whose value is 'Tutte le stagione' (the report's own case). Publish review: severity 'warning', publish allowed. Row readiness: state 'errors'. readinessFromSheet: 'blocked', which the chip explains as 'Required fields are missing or invalid — this scope cannot publish'. The cell shows a red blocking '!'. Same outcome for a deprecated eBay option and for a requirement that only a mapping rule's flag claims.
evidence: Throwaway test (studio-sheet harness with the mapping mocked to return errors [OFF] and findings [{rule:'offList'}]) printed: publishVerdict('EBAY', offList) = ['warn'], row readiness {state:'errors', issues:[{key:'stagione', severity:'error'}]}, readinessFromSheet(...).state = 'blocked'. Code: studio-sheet.service.ts:1639-1646 pushes severity 'error' for every mapped error; readiness-model.ts:74 maps any 'error' to 'blocked'; value-verdict.ts:56-63 returns 'warn' for eBay offList.
suggested_fix: Carry `findings` on MappedCell. Derive the readiness severity from publishVerdict(coordinate.channel, finding): 'block' becomes 'error', anything else 'warn'. Have CascadeCell draw the red mark only for blocking findings.

title: eBay listing-level values: variation rows show the listing's value, but their readiness is still judged on their own value (required-missing blocks the scope)
description: showEbayListingLevel runs after the row loop (studio-sheet.service.ts:1847-1851). By then each row's readiness issues (1618-1646) and completeness (1699) are already computed from that row's own value and its own mapped errors. The helper swaps the cell for the supplier's value and errors but never recomputes readiness. Publish skips a listing-level field on every row except the supplier (studio-publication-plan.ts:89-90). P1 also moves a variation's listing-level write to the parent and removes the row's copy (bulk-edit.service.ts:2398-2399). So this state is what every normal edit on a variation row now produces.
failure_scenario: GALE family on eBay IT. The parent listing stores Marca='Xavia'; the variations store none (for example after an operator set Marca on a variation row, which P1 moves to the parent), and no mapping rule fills Marca. On each variation row the Marca cell shows 'Xavia' with the listing-level mark and no errors. The row's readiness says 'Marca is required by eBay · IT' (state 'errors'), completeness counts Marca as missing, and the eBay scope chip reads 'Blocked'. The publish review raises no error and would send Marca='Xavia'.
evidence: Throwaway test (parent listing {Marca:'Xavia'}, child listing {}; child mapped cell with the error "Field 'Marca' is required.") printed: child cell {value:'Xavia', errors:[], listingLevel:{productId:'p', sku:'GALE', variation:true}}; child readiness {state:'errors', issues:[{key:'marca', message:'Marca is required by eBay · IT', severity:'error'}]}; completeness {filled:0, total:1, missing:[marca]}.
suggested_fix: For EBAY, work out the listing-level fields before building readiness. On rows that are not the supplier, skip those fields in both the issues and the completeness count, or judge them on the supplier's cell. That is the same rule readPublicationFacts applies (reporterOf).

title: Clearing a listing-level eBay aspect that a mapping fills does not clear it: eBay still gets the mapped value from the first variation; a parent override makes every variation 'hold another value' forever
description: The listing-level write model deals only with stored copies. A clear writes an explicit blank on the parent and INHERIT (removal) on every sibling (bulk-edit.service.ts:2379, 2398-2404). A variation without its own copy falls back to its mapping rule: masterDefaultRule, for example Marca from Master brand. The publisher takes the first row with a non-empty value (ebay-shared-listing-push.service.ts:204-229), the sheet's supplier does the same (ebay-listing-level.ts:65-68), and the parent's explicit blank is skipped. There is a second case with the same cause. When the parent stores an override that differs from the mapped value, every variation 'differs' (ebay-listing-level.ts:91, 164-165). The sheet then says 'This row also stores "Xavia", which eBay does not receive' although nothing is stored, and the publish review warns on each variation. The operator cannot clear that warning from the sheet, because any write on a variation row moves to the parent.
failure_scenario: Family LL-FAM on eBay IT with Master brand 'Xavia' and the parent listing storing Marca='Xavia Racing'. (1) Operator clears Marca on variation LL-FAM-A. Save succeeds; bags become parent {Marca:null}, A {}, B {}. resolveBatch gives parent null, A 'Xavia', B 'Xavia'. buildSharedListingInput sends itemSpecifics {Marca:'Xavia'} and the publish review says nothing. (2) Before the clear, the review said: 'Marca: eBay takes one value for the whole listing and will get "Xavia Racing" (from LL-FAM). 2 rows hold another value that is not sent: LL-FAM-A ("Xavia"), LL-FAM-B ("Xavia").' Neither variation stored a value.
evidence: Throwaway PGlite test on the ebay-listing-level-write harness, with Marca mapped from Master brand. It printed before [['LL-FAM','Xavia Racing','override'],['LL-FAM-A','Xavia','catalogRule'],['LL-FAM-B','Xavia','catalogRule']]; after the clear, bags {Marca:null} {Colore:'Rosso'} {Colore:'Giallo'}; resolved [null,'Xavia','Xavia']; eBay itemSpecifics {Marca:'Xavia'}; and the review warning quoted above.
suggested_fix: On a clear, write an explicit blank SET on every included sibling instead of INHERIT, so their mapping is stopped as well. Or have the publisher, the supplier logic and the review treat the parent's explicit stored blank as the listing's value. Compute 'differing' from stored own values (storedChannelState), not from rule-derived cell values, and do not say 'stores' for a mapped value.

title: A stored eBay item specific on a localizable column ('Stile') now outranks shared content, but the sheet still writes that column to content: a shared edit and a reset change nothing, and no column can remove the stored value
description: P1(d) drops the language-content hit whenever the listing's own itemSpecifics bag holds a non-blank value (resolve-batch.service.ts:358-361). The comment says the stored value 'is what the sheet edits (and resets)'. It is not. For a localizedContent column such as style, resolveWriteRouting always returns a content address, shared or pin (studio-sheet.service.ts:1287-1289; resolveWriteRouting at 643-676). The bulk save then sends every localizable change to applyContentBulk, which writes content tables and never platformAttributes.itemSpecifics (bulk-edit.service.ts:812-817). Only a PIN wins over the stored bag. The stored value cannot be reached any other way: otherItemSpecificColumns treats the name as covered by the style column and adds no 'Other item specifics' column for it (ebay-other-specifics.ts:27-30, 39). The cell also names its source from the content hit (Master or shared language) while showing the listing bag's value.
failure_scenario: GALE eBay IT listing with platformAttributes.itemSpecifics.Stile='Da motociclista'. The operator edits Stile on the eBay sheet to 'Sportivo' and picks 'Edit the shared Italian' in the acknowledgement. The save succeeds and writes the shared translation. On the next read the cell shows 'Da motociclista' again, and publish sends 'Da motociclista'. 'Reset to inherited' removes only a pin. Before #193 the shared edit won: content hid the stored bag, and the publisher overwrote itemSpecifics.Stile with the content value.
evidence: resolve-batch.service.ts:358-361 (the stored bag wins over non-pin content; the P1 test 'shows and sends the listing's own "Stile" over a computed shared value' pins this); studio-sheet.service.ts:1287-1289 and 643-676 (localizable means content routing, always); bulk-edit.service.ts:812-817 (localizable changes go to contentEdits and applyContentBulk); ebay-other-specifics.ts:27-30, 39 (covered names get no column); studio-publication-ebay.ts:149-153 (the publisher writes cell.value into itemSpecifics).
suggested_fix: When the listing stores its own non-blank value for a platformAttributes field, route that cell's write and reset to the bag (target channel, store path) instead of content, and label its source as the listing's value. Or keep content routing and have a shared or pin write also clear the stored bag entry. Either way, give the stored value a reset that removes it.

title: Publish still blocks on variation values eBay never receives (title, description, category): the 'one listing value' rule covers item specifics only
pr: pre-existing (P1 / report 5 I-2 goal only partly met by #193)
description: buildSharedListingInput takes title, description, category_id and condition from the parent row (`src = parentRow`, ebay-shared-listing-push.service.ts:181, 242-244). TradingVariation carries only sku, price, quantity, specifics and ean. readPublicationFacts skips a variation's cell only when its field is a listing-level item specific (line 90). It reports every other finding on every variation with the verdict (line 92), and 'length' blocks.
failure_scenario: eBay IT family. The parent listing's own title is 'Giacca GALE' (11 characters). The variations follow Master names of 92 characters. resolveBatch puts 'Title exceeds 80 characters (92).' with rule 'length' on LL-FAM-A and LL-FAM-B. The publish review shows two blocking errors and the publish is refused, although eBay would receive only the parent's 11-character title.
evidence: Throwaway PGlite test printed: TITLES [['LL-FAM','Giacca GALE',[]], ['LL-FAM-A','Giacca da moto GALE … variante A',['Title exceeds 80 characters (92).'],[{rule:'length'}]], ['LL-FAM-B', … same]]. studio-publication-plan.ts:89-93 pushes severity 'error' for 'length' on every row except listing-level item specifics.
suggested_fix: For an EBAY family, judge listing-level non-aspect fields (title, description, subtitle, category, condition, policies, item location) only on the row the builder reads (the parent), as is already done for item specifics through reporterOf.

title: Sheet import, xlsx catalogue import and channel-file import skip the listing-level rule: a variation's value is stored where eBay never reads it, and a parent clear leaves copies that eBay then sends
pr: #193 (P1.4 'saved where eBay reads it' met only on the bulk-save path)
description: Only the bulk save moves a listing-level item specific written on a variation row to the parent listing, and clears every copy on a clear (bulk-edit.service.ts:1576-1620, 2379-2404). The transfer planner patches the row's own listing (catalog-transfer-plan.ts:727, applied at catalog-transfer.service.ts:290). The product sheet's own Import uses the same planner and writer (sheet-import.service.ts:220, 374 applyTransferRecord). No transfer file uses ebay-listing-level.ts.
failure_scenario: (1) A sheet or xlsx import sets 'Paese di origine'='Italia' on variation LL-FAM-A of an eBay IT family whose parent stores 'Pakistan'. The import reports success and A's bag gets 'Italia'. eBay keeps receiving 'Pakistan', and the review only warns that A 'holds another value that is not sent'. This is report root cause #7, reintroduced on the import path. (2) An import CLEAR on the parent row of an aspect that variation A still stores as 'Cina': the parent becomes blank and eBay receives 'Cina'. The same clear typed in the sheet removes A's copy too.
evidence: catalog-transfer-plan.ts:716-729 (verdict, then a channelValuePatch on `working` = this row's own listing); catalog-transfer.service.ts:290 (updateMany on that listing id); sheet-import.service.ts:374; grep shows ebay-listing-level is used only by studio-sheet, studio-publication-plan and bulk-edit.
suggested_fix: Share the listing-level routing (parent move plus family clear) between bulk-edit and the transfer planner. At least give the import review a warning or refusal when a variation row's listing-level value will not be sent.

title: Shopify sheet editor still refuses off-list, over-limit and required-clear metafield values that the xlsx/CFI import now stores with a warning
pr: #193 (import moved to the verdict, the editor branch did not)
description: The bulk save's Shopify branch calls validateShopifyField or nativeFieldValueError and refuses the cell on any sentence (bulk-edit.service.ts:1046-1053). That includes 'Choose one of these values: …', max-length or max-number rules, and 'Enter a value. Shopify needs this field.' The transfer planner runs the same value through validateChannelValue, which turns these into 'offList' or 'schema' findings (validate-channel-value.ts:60-69). editVerdict stores them and adds 'Imported as written' (catalog-transfer-plan.ts:716-719). Both paths agree only at publish, where both block.
failure_scenario: A Shopify product metafield with choices ['Rouge','Bleu']. Typing or pasting 'Red' on the Shopify sheet is refused with 'Choose one of these values: Rouge, Bleu.' The same value in an Overrides row of an xlsx import is stored, with a warning. Clearing a required metafield behaves the same way: the editor refuses, the import stores.
evidence: bulk-edit.service.ts:1052-1053 `const error = … validateShopifyField(field.definition, raw) …; if (error) { errors.push(...); continue }`; validate-channel-value.ts:69 `findings.push(finding(isOffListError(error) ? 'offList' : 'schema', error))`; catalog-transfer-plan.ts:717 keeps only editVerdict 'refuse', which is 'type'.
suggested_fix: Split the Shopify branch the way validateChannelValue does: refuse only what cannot be stored (malformed JSON or type), push off-list, limit and required findings as warnings, and store the value.

title: A list on a single-value field: the editor refuses it as a type error, the xlsx (format=json) and channel-file import store it with a 'count' warning
description: value-verdict.ts:6-7 says 'a list sent to one value' is a type problem and is refused. checkForStorage does that on the bulk-save path ('takes ONE value — a list was sent', sheet-values.ts:312). validateChannelValue instead flattens a scalar field's array to its first member for the shape check and records a 'count' finding, which is stored (validate-channel-value.ts:74-78). The import applies that verdict (catalog-transfer-plan.ts:716-719), and the transfer file accepts JSON arrays (catalog-transfer-file.ts:54).
failure_scenario: An Overrides row: eBay IT, field Genere (SINGLE), format json, value ["Uomo","Donna"]. The import stores the array with the warning 'Genere takes one value; 2 are set.' Pasting or sending the same array through the sheet is refused. Publish then blocks on 'count'.
evidence: validate-channel-value.ts:74-78; sheet-values.ts:312; catalog-transfer-plan.ts:717 (only 'type' refuses).
suggested_fix: In validateChannelValue, return 'type' for a new write of an array with more than one member to a scalar field, keeping 'count' for reading legacy stored values. Or pass a flag from the write paths.

title: Clearing a required channel field: the editor warns 'required', the import clears it with no word
description: The editor's channel check re-resolves after the change and reports the required finding as a warning on the cell it wrote (information-validation.ts:57-76). The import calls only validateChannelValue(field, null). That adds no finding for a blank value, because the required check lives in resolveBatch, not in validateChannelValue.
failure_scenario: eBay IT Marca (required). A sheet Clear returns the warning "Marca: Field 'Marca' is required." An import CLEAR of Marca produces no warning in the import review. Both block at publish.
evidence: information-validation.ts:64-76 (a cleared cell this save wrote gets its warning); validate-channel-value.ts:81 (blank values add no shape finding); catalog-transfer-plan.ts:716-719.
suggested_fix: In the import, add a 'required' warning when a CLEAR or INHERIT empties a field with priority 'required', or reuse informationChangeErrors.

title: 'Other item specifics' over 65 characters are never blocked at publish on a single-product eBay listing, and the save answer carries no warning for them
description: Stored specifics that no category column serves are still sent (studio-publication-ebay.ts:148). ebayStoredSpecificIssues, which blocks a value over 65 characters, runs only when ebayAxes is set, that is for a family (lines 74-76, 101). A single-product listing skips it, and these columns have no resolved cell, so cellFindings never sees them. At edit time the bulk save drops maxLength for item specifics and skips capViolation (bulk-edit.service.ts:1064-1080), leaving the check to informationChangeErrors. That function only judges catalogue cells, and other_specific_* columns are not catalogue cells. Only the web's client-side length tint remains.
failure_scenario: A single-product eBay IT listing stores itemSpecifics {'Team name': <70 characters, no commas>}. It shows in 'Other item specifics'. Publish review: no issue. At send, eBay rejects the revise with 21919308, and the operator sees a generic Trading failure. The same value on a family listing is blocked in the review with the exact reason.
evidence: studio-publication-plan.ts:74 `ebayAxes = … included.length > 1 …`, :101 `if (ebayAxes && resolved[0]) … ebayStoredSpecificIssues`; bulk-edit.service.ts:1064-1066, 1080; information-validation.ts:57-60 (loops only resolveBatch cells).
suggested_fix: Run the stored-specific length check for single-product eBay listings too (rows = [parent]). Have the bulk save emit the 65-character finding for other_specific_* columns, which informationChangeErrors cannot see.

title: The publish review judges eBay item specifics that the active mapping excludes from sending
pr: pre-existing for catalogue cells; #193 for the new stored-specific check
description: buildEbayListingInput removes the specifics the active mapping version excludes (pushExclusionsCache: excluded.fieldKeys and excluded.specifics, lines 155-161) before sending. readPublicationFacts never consults the exclusions. It blocks on every finding of those cells (studio-publication-plan.ts:92), and ebayStoredSpecificIssues blocks a value over 65 characters in excluded stored specifics (line 136).
failure_scenario: The Owner excludes the 'Caratteristiche' item specific in the active eBay mapping, so the live listing keeps eBay's value. A variation-family parent stores a 90-character 'Caratteristiche' with no commas. The review blocks with 'eBay takes at most 65 characters per value', although the builder would drop the specific.
evidence: studio-publication-ebay.ts:155-161 vs studio-publication-plan.ts:84-101 (no exclusion lookup).
suggested_fix: Load the same exclusions in readPublicationFacts and skip findings or stored specifics that are excluded from sending.

title: Formula saves drop the save's verdict warnings and word their own differently from a typed value
description: A formula writes through PATCH /products/bulk, but the field writer returns only ok or error. The body's `warnings` (the channel verdict from informationChangeErrors: Ajv schema findings, required, count, eBay off-list) are discarded (lines 140-149). setCellFormula reports only the formula's own checks (cell-formula.service.ts:210, 516-535). These use different rules. A joined list over 65 characters on a single-value eBay aspect is flagged by raw length ('The result is 70 characters; X accepts 65.'), while the verdict says 'takes one value; eBay would receive 3 (…)'. The off-list text says 'the channel may refuse it at publish' for eBay, where publish only warns.
failure_scenario: ="A, B, C, …" (70 characters) on a single-value eBay aspect. The formula response warns about length. The same text typed in the cell warns that eBay would receive 3 values. A formula result that breaks an Amazon schema pattern is saved with no warning, while the same typed value comes back with one.
evidence: cell-formula.routes.ts:140-149 (body.warnings ignored); cell-formula.service.ts:210 and 527-535; validate-channel-value.ts:84-94.
suggested_fix: Return body.warnings from the field writer and merge them into setCellFormula's warnings, dropping duplicates. Build the formula's length and count check on validateChannelValue.

title: The record drawer's list input silently truncates each value at the column's maxLength (65 on eBay aspects)
description: The drawer's list control passes maxLength={column.maxLength} to each value's <Textarea>, so the browser cuts typing and paste at the cap. Every sheet editor instead stores the value, shows the count and warns: SlotListEditor 'never truncated', FormulaCellEditor 'nothing is ever truncated', and textLimitFor's NO_TEXT_LIMIT, which P1 added for exactly this rule.
failure_scenario: Pasting a 72-character value into a multi-value eBay aspect in the drawer stores the first 65 characters, with no warning. The same paste in the sheet's list editor stores 72 characters and warns.
evidence: AttributeShapeInput.tsx:39 `maxLength={column.maxLength ?? undefined}`; used by drawer/fields/RecordField.tsx:423; compare design-system/grid/editors/sheet.ts:65-72 (textLimitFor) and SlotListEditor.tsx:21.
suggested_fix: Drop the maxLength attribute (or pass textLimitFor) and show a counter with the over-limit state, as the sheet editors do.

title: A readiness refresh after an edit is thrown away, or overwritten, by a family-wide readiness read that started before the save
description: After a channel-only save, #194 sends only the coordinate read (`coordinateNonce`, lines 419-434). That read is merged only when `prev.status === 'ready'` (lines 428-430), so it is dropped while the family-wide read is still loading. It also never cancels or restarts a family read that is already running. The family read's effect (lines 436-550) does not depend on `coordinateNonce`. When it lands it sets `{status:'ready', byScope, matrix}` unconditionally (line 527), even though it read the index before the save committed. Before #194, `refreshReadiness()` bumped `askedNonce`. That re-ran this effect: the cleanup at 543-548 aborted the in-flight read and a fresh read was made after the save. The coordinate path removed that ordering.
failure_scenario:
1. Open GALE-JACKET · eBay · IT. The family-wide readiness read (11–13 MB raw) is still in flight, or a live-refresh read is in flight: every `listing.updated` SSE event anywhere in the business starts one (`useLiveRefresh`).
2. The sheet (compact, about 0.6 MB) is already editable. The operator fills a required field; it saves.
3. 800 ms later the only=coordinate answer arrives with EBAY 45%. If the family read has not landed yet, the answer is discarded. If it has, the answer is merged, but the older family read lands afterwards.
4. Either way, the family read replaces the chips and matrix with its pre-save snapshot (EBAY 40%, field still listed as missing).
5. The scope menu, the Shared dot, the Errors tab and the Variants projection keep the pre-edit numbers until the next save, Reload or 'Refresh progress'.
evidence: contracts.tsx:419-434 (the coordinate effect has deps `[coordinateNonce]` only and merges only if prev is ready); :457-460 (a family read keeps `ready` only across a refresh); :527 (the family answer lands unconditionally); :550 (the family effect's deps exclude coordinateNonce); :1081-1084 (a coordinate refresh bumps only coordinateNonce); useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:139-146 (every channel-only save asks `{coordinate:true}`). On origin/main, `refreshReadiness = () => setAskedNonce(n => n + 1)` re-ran and aborted the family read.
suggested_fix: Order the two reads. When a coordinate refresh is asked while a family read is in flight, abort that read and re-issue it; otherwise record the coordinate answer and re-apply it on top of any family answer that started earlier (compare start sequence numbers). Also keep a coordinate answer that lands while status is 'loading' and apply it once the family read lands.

title: On a channel scope, page load, Reload and every live refresh still read the whole family's readiness (11–13 MB); the plan's 50 KB budget and 'readiness for the open coordinate only' are not met
description: P2 item 4 says 'readiness for the open coordinate only', with the budget 'readiness ≤ 50 KB on a channel scope'. #194 uses `only=coordinate` only for the read after a save. The load read (line 465) is still the family-wide URL, with no `only` or `workspace=1`. The server then returns every coordinate of every channel. Its matrix is grouped over all family rows in every market, with `byProduct` and `optionalMissing` per product (scope-readiness.service.ts:74-77, 104-108). The same full read also runs on Reload, on 'Refresh progress', and on every live-refresh nonce. Any `listing.updated` or `listing.synced` event in the business triggers a live refresh, and those events are not filtered by product (contracts.tsx:593-605). The code comments state the size themselves.
failure_scenario:
Open GALE-JACKET · eBay · IT.
- The chips, Errors tab and Variants projection need one channel coordinate's matrix plus one small chip per channel.
- The page instead downloads about 11–13 MB raw of readiness. That is more than 200× the 50 KB budget.
- It downloads it again whenever a background sync emits a listing event anywhere in the business.
evidence: contracts.tsx:414-417 ('the family-wide read (every scope, every coordinate: 11 MB raw on GALE eBay IT) stays for the page load, a Reload and "Refresh progress"'); contracts.tsx:465 (`readinessUrl(productId, { market, locale, channel, listingId, accountId })`, no `only`); scope-readiness.service.ts:74-77 (whole-family findMany when `only` is null); :104-108 (matrix over all rows); readiness-only-coordinate.vitest.test.ts:1-5 ('the family-wide answer was 13.1 MB … The default answer is unchanged'); REPORT-2026-09-30.md P2 item 4 and its budgets.
suggested_fix: On a channel scope, ask for the chips of every channel without matrix detail, plus the open coordinate's matrix (for example `only=coordinate` combined with a chips-only summary for the other scopes). Keep the family-wide read for the Shared scope and for an explicit 'Refresh progress'.

title: The page-load prefetch never runs on the main way into the studio: links from the product list carry no query string
description: `studioPrefetchPlan` returns no reads unless the URL names `market`, and for the sheet it also needs `locale`/`locales` (plus `account` on a channel scope). The product list builds its editor link as `/products/${row.id}/edit/studio` with no query, and the Listings workspace does the same. So on the most common navigation, neither the destination nor the sheet is prefetched: the sheet still waits for the frame's product, marketplaces and connections reads. The studio later writes a market into the URL only when the remembered market differs from the default (contracts.tsx:888-894), so a reload of that page usually still has no market. The docblock's premise, 'Most loads name everything in the URL', does not hold for the default entry path. P2 item 1, 'product, destination and sheet start together', is therefore met only for deep links.
failure_scenario:
1. The operator clicks a product in /products, which opens `/products/P/edit/studio`.
2. `prefetchStudio` sees no `market` and starts nothing.
3. The master sheet read starts only after `loadStudioData` has resolved the markets and the provider has derived market and locale: one full serial hop more than a deep link.
4. Reloading the page gives the same result.
evidence: studioPrefetch.ts:85-108 (line 88: `if (!productId || !market) return none`; line 100: the master sheet also needs `locale`; line 106: a channel scope needs `account && locale`); apps/web/src/app/products/next/columns.tsx:170 (`const editHref = (row) => `/products/${row.id}/edit/studio``); apps/web/src/app/products/page.tsx renders ProductsNextClient; ListingsWorkspace.tsx:2420 and :3929 (the same bare link); contracts.tsx:888-894 (the remembered market is written only when it differs from the default).
suggested_fix: Put the resolved market and locale in the list links (the studio already remembers the last market and languages), or let the prefetch use the same remembered or default market and language rules the provider applies, adopting only when they match. Alternatively, let the sheet route default market and locale on the server.

title: A studio tab whose code fails to load replaces the whole studio with the app-wide error page, and 'Try again' cannot recover
description: #194 makes each tab a `next/dynamic` chunk. The chunks are created once at module scope (lines 38-40). `next/dynamic` wraps its loader in a single `React.lazy` (node_modules/next/dist/shared/lib/lazy-dynamic/loadable.js). React.lazy caches a rejected import and throws the same error on every later render. There is no error boundary inside the studio: the only boundary above it is apps/web/src/app/error.tsx. Before #194 every tab was part of the studio's own chunk, so a tab switch could not fail this way.
failure_scenario:
1. The operator has the studio open on the Sheet tab.
2. A new build is deployed (Railway/Vercel serve only the new chunk hashes), or the network drops.
3. The operator clicks 'Images'. The dynamic import rejects (ChunkLoadError).
4. The studio frame (scope bar, save status, tabs) is replaced by 'Something went wrong – Loading chunk … failed'.
5. 'Try again' re-renders the same lazy component, which throws the cached error again. Only a full page reload recovers.
evidence: StudioTabHost.tsx:38-40 (`dynamic(STUDIO_TAB_LOADERS[id], { loading })` at module scope); studioTabs.ts:14-27; loadable.js: `const Lazy = lazy(() => opts.loader().then(convertModule))`, created once per dynamic() call; `find apps/web/src/app -name error.tsx` → only app/error.tsx, dashboard/overview and pricing; app/error.tsx calls `reset`.
suggested_fix: Wrap `<Surface>` in a studio-level error boundary that shows the tab's own error with a 'Reload tab' action. On retry, recreate the dynamic component (keep it in state, or use a loader wrapper that retries the import), or fall back to `location.reload()` for a ChunkLoadError.

title: A save that touches the Shared record gets only a coordinate readiness read when an earlier save's timer fires while it is still in flight
description: `readinessForFamily.current = true` is set when a Shared-touching save starts (line 328, before `await commitChannelRow`). The debounce callback reads the flag and clears it (lines 140-145). If an earlier save's 800 ms timer fires while the Shared-touching save B is still in flight, the family read runs before B commits and the flag is cleared. When B settles, `refreshReadinessSoonRef` arms a new timer with the flag false. B's effect on the Shared chip and on every channel that follows Master is then read only for the open coordinate.
failure_scenario:
1. On the eBay IT sheet, the operator edits a listing-only cell on row 1; it settles and a timer is set for +800 ms.
2. Within that window they edit a cell that writes the Shared record (a Master field, or content saved to every channel) on row 2. B's commit is in flight when the timer fires.
3. The family read runs, before B commits.
4. B settles; the next timer sees the flag false and sends only `only=coordinate`.
5. The Shared chip and the Amazon/Shopify chips keep their pre-B numbers until a Reload.
evidence: useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:135-146 (the flag is read and reset inside the timer); :327-328 (`const save = rowSettle(req); if (save.touchesMaster()) readinessForFamily.current = true;` before the await); :392 and :402 (`refreshReadinessSoonRef.current()` in onReconciled/onSettled); saveSettle.ts:38-40.
suggested_fix: Set the family flag when a Shared-touching save settles successfully (inside onSettled or onReconciled for that request), not when it starts. Alternatively, count in-flight Shared-touching saves and make the timer ask for the family read whenever one settled after the last family read began.

title: Merging a coordinate read moves that coordinate's readiness rows to the end of the matrix, so the Errors tab tables reorder after every save
description: The server sorts the matrix: Shared first, then by coordinateKey and language order (scope-readiness.service.ts:104-108). `mergeCoordinateReadiness` removes the refreshed coordinate's entries and appends the fresh ones at the end. ReadinessPanel groups rows and derives its language columns in array order (ReadinessPanel.tsx:25-39). A Reload therefore shows one order, and each channel save shows another.
failure_scenario:
1. Family with Amazon IT and eBay IT; the Errors tab lists Shared, Amazon · IT, eBay · IT.
2. Save a cell on the Amazon IT sheet, then open Errors.
3. 'Readiness by language' and 'Needs attention' now list Amazon · IT after eBay · IT. A channel-only language column (for example nl/fr from Amazon BE) can also change position.
4. After a Reload the order returns.
evidence: readiness.ts:136 (`[...previous.matrix.filter(...), ...fresh]`); scope-readiness.service.ts:107-108 (the server sort); ReadinessPanel.tsx:25-31 (`languages = [...new Set(entries.map(...))]`, grouped Map in array order).
suggested_fix: Replace the entries in place (map over previous.matrix, substituting by key, then add genuinely new keys), or re-sort with the server's comparator after merging.

title: A formula save never refreshes readiness, on the Master or a channel sheet
description: `useCellFormulas` reports a settled formula save through `onSettled`. On Master that is only the sheet's quiet `refresh` (line 150). On a channel sheet it is only `refresh(...)` of the rows (useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:237). Neither calls `refreshReadinessSoon` / `refreshReadiness`. A formula save or replace writes the cell's value through the bulk path inside a transaction (`emitManyTx`, no SSE), so the live refresh does not fire either. The chips stay at the old numbers.
failure_scenario:
1. On the Shared sheet, type `="Xavia Racing"` into an empty required Brand cell.
2. The value is stored and shown in the cell.
3. The Shared/channel chips and the per-coordinate readiness columns still count Brand as missing until another plain save, Reload or 'Refresh progress'.
evidence: useMasterSheetAdapter.tsx:150 (`onSettled: refresh`); useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:237 (`onSettled: () => { void refresh(...) }`); useCellFormulas.ts:147-151 (the queue settle calls only `onSettled`); product-event.service.ts:196-207 (`emitManyTx` publishes no SSE); bulk-edit.service.ts:416 (bulk edits always run in a transaction).
suggested_fix: Call the same debounced readiness refresh from the formula `onSettled` or `onValueSaved` path: a coordinate refresh on a channel sheet, the family read on Master.

title: Measure editor erases the stored number when the operator types or pastes the unit with it ("1.5 kg", "12kg", "9 OUNCE")
description: #186 turned the value field into `type="text"` (line 79). `onText` (53-58) sends every string that `Number()` cannot parse as `value: null` and reports `{ value: null, unit }` on each keystroke. Enter, Tab or a click away then saves that. The server accepts `{ value: null, unit }` with no finding (apps/api/src/services/pim/sheet-values.ts:299-309). A grid paste of the same text parses correctly: `parseShape` (shapeValue.ts:16-25), whose own comment says "Do not turn an invalid member into null".
failure_scenario: An Amazon item_weight cell shows "1.2 kg" ({1.2, kilograms}). The operator selects it and types "1.5 kg" (the first key "1" opens the editor, ".5 kg" follows), then presses Enter. The save sends {value: null, unit: 'kilograms'}. The weight is gone, no warning is shown, and the listing is published without it. The same happens for "12kg", for pasting "9 OUNCE" into the open field, and for typing "-" and then clicking away.
evidence: Audit test (a throwaway `*.audit-tmp.vitest.test.ts`, now deleted) rendered MeasureEditor with value {12,'KG'} and called Input.onChange with the text. Results: '12kg' → onValueChange({value:null,unit:'KG'}); '9 OUNCE' → {value:null,unit:'KG'}; '1.5 cm' → {value:null,unit:'KG'}. For the same strings parseShape('measure', …) gives {12,'KG'}, {9,'OUNCE'} and {1.5,'CM'}. The switch to type="text" came in 46f113479 (the #186 code-review fixes).
suggested_fix: Parse the field with asMeasure/parseShape: take a trailing unit when it matches `unitOptions`. When the text is still not a number, report the raw string so the server refuses it with "… is not a number", or keep the last valid value and mark the field invalid. Never report null for non-empty text.

title: Escape in the measure editor's unit list saves the abandoned edit instead of cancelling it
description: `onCancel={() => stopEditing(true)}` assumes the argument means cancel. In AG 36 the editor param is `stopEditing(suppressNavigateAfterEdit?, event?)`; it stops with source 'api', and `shouldStop` treats that as a commit. AG's own Escape cancel is deferred with setTimeout. ListboxPanel's bubble Escape handler (ListboxPanel.tsx:313) runs synchronously first, so the value the editor last reported is committed. #186 made the unit list reachable by keyboard (Tab from the number field, lines 68-76), which opens this path.
failure_scenario: A weight cell holds {12, kilograms}. The operator opens it, types 3, Tabs to the units, arrows to grams, changes their mind and presses Escape. {3, grams} is saved, though the key line says "Esc cancels". With more than 8 units, Escape from the unit search field does the same.
evidence: ag-grid-community main.cjs.js:42532-42537: `stopEditing: (suppressNavigateAfterEdit, event) => editSvc.stopEditing(position, { source: 'api', suppressNavigateAfterEdit, event })`, with no cancel. :44844-44846: source 'api' → shouldStop returns true. :29823-29833: onEscapeKeyDown runs `setTimeout(() => stopEditing(cellCtrl, { cancel: true }))`. ag-grid-react index.cjs.js:2542 portals the editor into the `.ag-popup-editor` element. AG's keydown listener was registered there first, so React's bubble handlers run after it but in the same dispatch, before AG's deferred cancel.
suggested_fix: For cancel paths, call the grid API's `props.api.stopEditing(true)` (a real cancel), or do nothing on Escape and let AG's cancel run. Fix the `stopEditing: (cancel?: boolean)` typings in MeasureEditor, ListPanelEditor, ChannelCategoryEditor, ReferenceSelectEditor and EbayPolicyEditor. In those editors it is harmless today only because the reported value is unchanged when they cancel.

title: Enter behaves differently by editor kind: lists save and move down, text, number, reference and category cells save and stay
description: #186 has SelectPanelEditor report on Enter and lets AG end the edit. AG then applies `enterNavigatesVerticallyAfterEdit` (GridSheet.tsx:107) and moves down. MeasureEditor and ListPanelEditor behave the same way. The text, number and long-text editor ends Enter with `props.stopEditing()` and no event (FormulaCellEditor.tsx:337, or api.stopEditing at 301), so AG's navigateAfterEdit (main.cjs.js:43753-43770) does not move. AsyncListboxPanel (reference, eBay/Etsy category, Amazon product type) handles Enter itself with stopPropagation and ends it with `stopEditing()`, so it stays too. The comment at SelectPanelEditor.tsx:110-116 says AG "moves as it does for every other cell", which is not true.
failure_scenario: A keyboard operator works down a column. In the eBay Colore (select) column, Enter saves and moves to the next row. In Title, Price or the eBay category column, Enter saves and stays. The next keystroke, meant for the row below, overwrites the cell just saved. Two list kinds on the same sheet (Colore and Shipping template) also disagree.
evidence: apps/web/tests/sheet-select-keys.spec.ts:75-91 asserts that a list Enter moves to row 2. FormulaCellEditor.tsx:347-348 (Enter → save) and :337 (`props.stopEditing()` with no event). AsyncListboxPanel.tsx:56-60. ChannelCategoryEditor.tsx:38-42. GridSheet.tsx:82 states the sheet contract: "Enter commits and moves DOWN".
suggested_fix: Choose one behaviour for every editor. To move down everywhere, pass the keydown event through `props.stopEditing(false, event)` in FormulaCellEditor.save and in the AsyncListboxPanel-based editors. To stay everywhere, have lists call `stopEditing(true)` themselves on Enter. Cover it with one key-ownership test across all editor kinds.

title: Free-text list editor (Etsy tags and materials, eBay free-text multi-value item specifics) still loses the first typed key
description: P0 item 4 says typing into a selected cell keeps the first character in every editor. #186 passes `typedStart(eventKey)` only to the OptionList branch (line 88). The free-text branch (no options) renders `TagInput`, which starts with an empty input (primitives/TagInput.tsx:20) and receives nothing. AG consumed the keystroke to start the edit, so it is lost. The same editor also splits a pasted "a | b" into one tag, where a grid paste gives two values (shapeValue.ts:12).
failure_scenario: An Etsy Tags cell (list, max 13 > SLOT_COLUMNS_MAX 10, no options), a list-valued eBay "Other item specifics" column (ebay-other-specifics.ts builds shape 'list' with no options), or an eBay MULTI FREE_TEXT aspect with no suggested values. The operator selects the cell and types "Rosso". The editor opens with "osso", and Enter saves the tag "osso".
evidence: ListPanelEditor.tsx:87-92: `closed ? <OptionList … initialQuery={typedStart(props.eventKey)} /> : <TagInput value={items} … />`, so TagInput gets no eventKey. TagInput.tsx:20 `const [input, setInput] = useState('')`.
suggested_fix: Give TagInput an initial draft (for example `initialInput`), seed it with `typedStart(props.eventKey)`, and report it with `onDraft` so Enter saves it. Add this editor to the key-ownership test.

title: Open multi-value lists (eBay MULTI item specifics with suggestions) cannot take a typed value, in the editor or in "Set every row…"
description: P0 item 5 says open lists take a typed value. `shapeEditorSpec` (shapeColumn.ts:53-62) never passes the column's `mode`, so ListPanelEditor with options is always a closed OptionList: it has no "Use …" row, and a search with no match shows "No matches". A stored off-list value is labelled "(not in the list)" as if it were a fault, and is appended at the bottom. SelectPanelEditor shows it first, labelled "current". #193's SetColumnDialog offers "Or your own value" only for non-list choices (SheetControlDialogs.tsx:59, 79).
failure_scenario: On eBay IT an aspect with cardinality MULTI, aspectMode FREE_TEXT and suggested values becomes shape 'list', mode 'open' (channel-specs/ebay.ts:171-191). Example: Caratteristiche. The operator opens it and types "Protezioni CE" in the search. They get "No matches" and have no way to add the value. "Set every row…" offers only the checkbox list. Only a clipboard paste stores it.
evidence: shapeColumn.ts:53-62 (params: options, maxItems, label; no mode). ListPanelEditor.tsx:71-73 (`closed` depends only on options; off-list values appended with "(not in the list)"). SheetControlDialogs.tsx:59 (`choice = !list && …`), :62-64 (the list branch has no own-value field).
suggested_fix: Pass `mode` through shapeEditorSpec. When the list is open, show an "Add \"…\"" row (or make Enter in the search add the typed text as a chip), and label stored off-list values "current" as SelectPanelEditor does. Add the own-value field to SetColumnDialog for open list columns.

title: eBay business-policy cells (shipping, payment, return) have no keyboard path
description: P0 item 2 says every popup list editor owns Enter, Tab, arrows and Escape. EbayPolicyEditor renders a native `<Select>` with no autoFocus and no key handling. AG leaves focus on the grid cell when an editor has no focusIn (main.cjs.js:44802-44811). While editing, arrows are ignored (29705-29708) and Tab is AG's (save and move). The one-click chevron #186 added also opens this editor, because the policy keys are reference fields (CascadeCell.tsx:139). channelColumns.tsx:89 routes these columns here before the keyboard-capable ReferenceSelectEditor.
failure_scenario: A keyboard-only operator on eBay IT focuses the Shipping policy cell and presses Enter, and the popup opens. ArrowDown does nothing. Tab closes it without a choice and moves right. Typing a letter does nothing. The policy can be set only with the mouse.
evidence: EbayPolicyInput.tsx:23 (`<Select …>` with no autoFocus), :34-41 (only Escape is handled). channelColumns.tsx:89-90. reference-values.ts:7-9 (fulfillmentPolicyId, paymentPolicyId and returnPolicyId are REFERENCE_FIELDS, so the chevron is drawn).
suggested_fix: Route the policy fields to ReferenceSelectEditor or AsyncListboxPanel, which already own the keys, report Tab and focus their input. Or autofocus the select and forward Enter/Tab through onKeyChoice.

title: Ctrl/Cmd+Enter in a list writes the choice into every selected cell of every column, with no fence and no confirmation
description: The capture handler reports the choice on any Enter, modifiers included, and then lets AG handle the key. For Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, AG's onEnterKeyDown calls `applyBulkEdit` over every cell in every column of the selected ranges, running each column's parser. These writes are not fenced as one operation: operationFence has no bulkEditing hooks, so each cell is its own save and its own undo step. Text cells do not do this: suppressFormulaKeys gives Enter to FormulaCellEditor, so Cmd+Enter there saves one cell.
failure_scenario: The operator selects B2:D20 (Colore, Title, Brand), presses Enter on B2, arrows to "Nero" and presses Cmd+Enter. "Nero" is written into 57 cells, including every Title and Brand in the range. There is no confirmation, unlike "Set every row…", and there are many saves and undo steps.
