evidence: ListboxPanel.tsx:305-311 (no modifier check). main.cjs.js:29770 (`if (isCtrlEnter(event)) editSvc.applyBulkEdit(…)`) and 44513-44590 (the loop over `range.columns` sets each editable cell). bulkOperation.ts:173-183 (fill, paste, undo and delete are fenced; bulk edit is not).
suggested_fix: Ignore Enter with ctrl or meta in onKeyChoice and suppress Ctrl+Enter in the list columns' suppressKeyboardEvent. Or fence `bulkEditingStarted`/`bulkEditingStopped` and ask first, as "Set every row…" does.

title: A punctuation first key followed by Enter replaces the stored list value with option 1 (the Space fix is incomplete)
description: `typedStart` drops only whitespace, and its comment says why: "A space would start a search that highlights row 1, so Space then Enter replaced the stored value". `normalizeForSearch` drops every non-alphanumeric character, so a query like "-", ".", "/", "'", "&" or "#" has no tokens and `searchOptions` returns all options. ListboxPanel then highlights `bestMatch` (row 0, or row 1 when a "Use …" row exists), and Enter or Tab commits it.
failure_scenario: An eBay Stagione cell (strict) holds "Inverno". The operator types "-" (a spreadsheet placeholder habit) and presses Enter. "Estate" is saved. In an open list, "&" then Enter saves the first option, not "&".
evidence: Audit test (a throwaway `*.audit-tmp.vitest.test.ts`, now deleted) with the listboxPanelKeys harness: options Estate/Inverno/Tutte le stagione, value 'Inverno', initialQuery typedStart(k), then capture Enter. For '-', '.', '/', "'", '&' and '#', onKeyChoice('Estate'). For ' ', onKeyChoice('Inverno'). For an open list with '&', 'Estate'. option-search.ts:25-31 and 82-83; ListboxPanel.tsx:205.
suggested_fix: When `searchTokens(q)` is empty, treat the query as empty: keep `selectedIndex` (or -1) and do not jump to bestMatch. Or return '' from typedStart for keys with no search token.

title: Not every list has Clear: boolean cells and the reference, category and product-type pickers have none, and the empty row's label differs by editor
description: The plan says every list has "Clear". Channel select columns get `emptyLabel: SELECT_CLEAR_LABEL`, but channel boolean columns do not (params `{ options: BOOLEAN_OPTIONS }`, and the static selectEditor sets `emptyLabel: undefined`, SelectCellEditor.tsx:137). Master boolean columns have the same gap (columns.tsx:566-577). AsyncListboxPanel (eBay/Etsy category, Amazon product type, Etsy and Amazon reference fields) has no empty row at all. Where an empty row exists, its label varies: "Clear" in the grid, "Empty" in Set every row, "No units" in the measure editor, "No policy selected" in the policy editor. On an empty cell, the "Clear" row is marked as the selected option (`aria-selected={!value}`).
failure_scenario: An operator sets Amazon "is_heat_sensitive" (boolean) to Yes by mistake and opens the list to undo it. Only Yes and No are offered. The same is true for an Etsy shop section or an eBay category they want to remove. The only route is Delete, which then asks a question.
evidence: channelColumns.tsx:111-115; columns.tsx:566-577 (the boolean formula selector has params `{ options: BOOLEAN_OPTIONS }`); AsyncListboxPanel.tsx:82-85 (no emptyLabel passed to ListboxPanel); SheetControlDialogs.tsx:66 (emptyLabel="Empty"); ListboxPanel.tsx:339.
suggested_fix: Pass `emptyLabel: SELECT_CLEAR_LABEL` to boolean list editors on both sheets, add an optional Clear row to AsyncListboxPanel, and use one label everywhere.

title: A list's Clear hides the inherited value without the question Delete asks
description: #193 makes Delete ask "Clear or Reset to inherited" on every channel row and every Master variation, because a clear "stores an empty value in each cell: the value it inherits no longer shows" (sheetReset.ts:177-179, 223). The Clear row #186 added to every select list writes that same explicit blank through the same valueSetter (optimisticCell, pinned). It does not ask, and the list offers no reset row.
failure_scenario: On the eBay IT sheet, a Materiale cell inherits "Pelle" from Master. The operator opens the list and clicks "Clear", expecting to drop a listing override. The listing now stores a blank, Master's value no longer shows, and nothing said so. Delete on the same cell would have asked first.
evidence: channelColumns.tsx:108 (`emptyLabel: SELECT_CLEAR_LABEL`); SelectPanelEditor.tsx:91-104 (onCommit('') → onValueChange(null)); useSheetControl.tsx:125-138 and sheetReset.ts:177-179, 220-228 (the Delete path asks when the change hides an inherited value).
suggested_fix: Where the cell inherits a value, offer "Reset to inherited" beside "Clear" in the list, or word the row "Clear (hide inherited value)" and route it through the same question.

title: An IME-confirming Enter closes the list (SelectPanelEditor) or commits the highlighted choice (category, product-type and reference pickers)
description: ListboxPanel skips reporting while `isComposing` (line 306), but AG's popup listener still gets the Enter and its onEnterKeyDown never checks composition. The list closes with the stored value and the cursor moves down, in the middle of the operator's search. AsyncListboxPanel's Enter handler has no `isComposing` check at all, so it commits the highlighted choice for a partly composed query. Text cells handle composition correctly (FormulaCellEditor.tsx:342). Separately, with an IME active a selected cell never opens by typing, because AG starts editing only on single-character keys and not on 'Process'.
failure_scenario: On macOS Chrome, a Japanese-IME operator types in the eBay category or reference search and presses Enter to confirm the conversion. The first result for the partial query is saved. In a select list, the same Enter closes the list unchanged and moves to the next row.
evidence: ListboxPanel.tsx:306; AsyncListboxPanel.tsx:56-60 (no isComposing check); main.cjs.js:29754-29790 (onEnterKeyDown has no composition check).
suggested_fix: Return early on `event.nativeEvent.isComposing` in AsyncListboxPanel. In the list columns' suppressKeyboardEvent, return true for Enter while `event.isComposing`, so AG does not end the edit.

title: Searchable grid lists are not announced: no aria-activedescendant, an unnamed listbox, and an input inside role=listbox
description: When ListboxPanel owns its search field, focus stays in that input and ↑/↓ move only a `.active` class. The input has no role=combobox, aria-controls or aria-activedescendant, and SelectPanelEditor passes neither `idPrefix` nor `ariaLabel`, so options have no ids and the listbox has no name. The input and the "No matches" div sit inside the role=listbox container. #186 widens the problem: every open list, and every list opened by typing, now uses this searching mode (`ownsSearch` includes allowCustom and initialQuery).
failure_scenario: A screen-reader user opens the eBay Brand list (open), types "X" and arrows through the matches. Nothing is announced, and Enter commits an option they never heard.
evidence: ListboxPanel.tsx:183 (ownsSearch), :292-304 (role=listbox container), :331-336 (search input, aria-label "Search options" only); SelectPanelEditor.tsx:137-145 (no idPrefix or ariaLabel). AsyncListboxPanel.tsx:73-75 shows the correct combobox pattern.
suggested_fix: When `ownsSearch`, make the input a combobox with aria-controls and aria-activedescendant pointing at `${id}-o${active}`. Render it outside the role=listbox element. Name the list from the column header.

title: Home, End, PageUp and PageDown are not handled in any list editor
description: ListboxPanel, AsyncListboxPanel and ListPanelEditor handle only ↑/↓, Enter, Tab and Escape. AG's popup listener does not handle page keys while editing. So PageDown and PageUp scroll the panel natively without moving the highlight, and Home and End move the caret in the search field. This is the same in every editor kind, but none meets the lens's Home/End/PageUp/PageDown requirement.
failure_scenario: In a 244-option eBay list, the operator presses PageDown twice. The view scrolls but the highlight stays on row 3. Enter then commits the off-screen row 3.
evidence: ListboxPanel.tsx:312-329; AsyncListboxPanel.tsx:52-71; ListPanelEditor.tsx:76-84; main.cjs.js:29675-29703 (the `_onCellKeyDown` switch has no page keys).
suggested_fix: Add Home, End, PageUp and PageDown to ListboxPanel (moving by the visible row count) and to AsyncListboxPanel. Reuse the `media-choice.ts` ListKey logic that already exists in the DS.

title: The one-click chevron on a locked list cell does nothing and gives no reason
description: #186 gives the chevron `pointer-events: auto; cursor: pointer` and an onClick that calls `api.startEditingCell`. That call silently does nothing on a non-editable cell (main.cjs.js:43032). The chevron is drawn on locked cells too (columns.tsx:499-503, CascadeCell.tsx:139). Enter, typing or a double-click on the same locked cell announce the refusal reason (useProductSheetInteraction.ts:73-78). A click on the chevron does not.
failure_scenario: On a variation row, the operator clicks the chevron of a per-variant axis cell the parent does not hold, or of a `writable: false` alias cell. The cursor shows a pointer, nothing opens, and no reason is given. A double-click on the same cell explains why.
evidence: SelectCellEditor.tsx:96-109; grid.css:626-629; useProductSheetInteraction.ts:59-66 and 73-78.
suggested_fix: Draw the action chevron only when the cell is editable. Otherwise, route the click to the same explainRefusal the double-click uses.

title: Measure editor with more than 8 units: Tab lands on the unit list's container, not its search field
description: `tabToUnits` focuses `.nds-listbox-pop`, the ListboxPanel container. With more than 8 units, ListboxPanel renders its own search input (`ownsSearch`), but focus is not placed in it. Typed letters then go nowhere. Only the arrows work, and the operator must click to search.
failure_scenario: Amazon length units (centimeters, decimeters, feet, inches, meters, millimeters, …) exceed 8. The operator types 12, Tabs, and types "mil" to find millimeters. Nothing filters.
evidence: MeasureEditor.tsx:70-75 (`units.focus()` on the container); ListboxPanel.tsx:183 (ownsSearch when options.length > 8), :331-336.
suggested_fix: Focus `units.querySelector('.nds-combo-search input') ?? units`.

title: In an open list, Enter saves a longer option instead of the value the operator fully typed
description: With allowCustom, the typed text becomes the "Use …" row at index 0, but the highlight starts on `bestMatch` (index 1) whenever any option contains the typed tokens. A complete value that is a prefix or word of a longer option therefore cannot be saved with Enter or Tab; it needs ↑ first. SetColumnDialog makes this choice explicit with a separate own-value field.
failure_scenario: The open eBay Materiale list offers "Cotone biologico". The operator types "Cotone" and presses Enter. "Cotone biologico" is saved. The same happens with Brand "Xavia Racing" when the list holds "Xavia Racing Team".
evidence: ListboxPanel.tsx:193-199 (custom first, `bestMatch = custom && listed.length ? 1 : 0`) and :205. The prop doc at :130-135 states this is intended ("Enter takes Nero for Ner, ↑ takes the typed text").
suggested_fix: When the typed text has no exact match and the operator has typed at least a whole word, highlight the "Use …" row. Or make Tab take the typed text and Enter take the best match, and state that in the key line.

title: The design-system CHANGELOG says the "Use …" row is offered LAST; the code puts it FIRST
description: The P0 entry reads: "allowCustom (the typed text is offered LAST as `Use "…"`…)". The code-review fix 46f113479 moved the row to the top (ListboxPanel.tsx:131-134, `matches = custom ? [custom, ...listed] : listed` at 197) and did not update the entry. The Factory CHANGELOG mirrors the same wording.
failure_scenario: Someone building on the DS reads the CHANGELOG, expects the typed row at the bottom, and writes tests or keyboard logic (for example End to reach it) against the wrong order.
evidence: CHANGELOG.md:43 versus ListboxPanel.tsx:130-135 and 197; `git log -S'It is the FIRST row'` → 46f113479.
suggested_fix: Change "LAST" to "FIRST (the best match stays highlighted)" in both CHANGELOGs.

title: Factory design-system drift: committed .d.ts declarations for 14 modules the stack changed still describe the old API
description: All 17 design-system source files the stack touched are byte-identical between apps/web and apps/factory. CHANGELOG wording differs on purpose, and the components.css differences lie outside the stack's hunks and pre-exist. But factory also tracks 194 declaration files. The stack updated one of them (FormulaCellEditor.d.ts) and left the declarations stale for ListboxPanel, AsyncListboxPanel, OptionList, SourceIndicator, ListPanelEditor, MeasureEditor, SelectCellEditor, SelectPanelEditor, selectPanelModel, roundTrip, sheet, sheetWriter, editors/index and primitives/Tooltip. check-ds-dts-fresh.mjs notes that sessions are told to read these declarations.
failure_scenario: A factory session planning from `SelectCellEditor.d.ts` sees `SelectChevron(): JSX.Element` with no `onOpen`. `ListboxPanel.d.ts` lacks onKeyChoice, initialQuery and allowCustom. `selectPanelModel.d.ts` lacks typedStart and withStoredValue. `index.d.ts` does not export openCellEditor, SELECT_CLEAR_LABEL, saveNote or textLimitFor.
evidence: `diff -q` over every touched file: all SAME. `git log -1` on the 14 factory .d.ts files → 3161da57b (a checkpoint). Only FormulaCellEditor.d.ts appears in `git diff origin/main HEAD -- apps/factory`. Examples: SelectCellEditor.d.ts:38 and index.d.ts:19.
suggested_fix: Regenerate the factory declarations for the touched modules (or all of them) in the same PR as the source change, or stop tracking them in factory as web already does.

title: Save-status recount scans rows × columns on every writer event: 1.8 s of main-thread work for a 105×5 paste
description: `refreshCounts` is subscribed to the SheetWriter and runs synchronously on every `emit()`. It walks every row × every column through `tracker.get` (a string key per call) and then iterates all tracker entries for `warnedCount`. SheetWriter emits once per queued cell (`set`, sheetWriter.ts:656) and once per settled row (`settle`, :876). A paste therefore costs O(cells × rows × columns). #194 added `sameStatus` to skip the re-render, but the scan itself still runs on every emit.
failure_scenario: Paste 105 rows × 5 columns on the channel sheet (60 columns). The writer emits 631 times (525 sets + 1 flush + 105 row settles), and each emit scans 6,300 cells. The browser main thread is blocked ~1.8 s (measured). For a 105 × 1 paste it is ~0.6 s. This alone consumes most of the 105-row paste budget of 3 s and shows up as long tasks while the paste answer lands.
evidence: Audit test (deleted) with the real SheetWriter (commitBatch) and CellSaveTracker and the verbatim refreshCounts body: `emits=631 realRecountMsForAllEmits=1771` for 105 rows × 5 cells and 60 columns. sheetWriter.ts:644-658 (emit per set), :900-960 (settle loop), :876 (emit per row).
suggested_fix: Keep refused and warned counts incrementally in CellSaveTracker (update them on set/clear), or coalesce recounts to one per microtask or animation frame. At minimum, hoist `productSheetRowKey(row)` out of the inner loop and iterate only the tracker's refused entries.

title: Master sheet still reloads the whole sheet and the family-wide readiness after every edit, and rebuilds every column twice
pr: pre-existing (P2 item 3 not applied to Master by #194)
description: Plan P2.3 says the save answer should patch the edited rows, with no sheet, readiness or reference reload. #194 applied this only to the channel sheet. On Master, `onSettled`/`onReconciled` still set `quietRead` and bump the nonce after every confirmed save, which triggers a full compact sheet read that replaces every row. The adapter also calls `refreshReadinessSoon()` → `refreshReadiness()` with no coordinate option, which re-reads the family-wide readiness. `attributeColumns` depends on `sheet` (line 363), so the sheet read rebuilds every ColDef. 800 ms later the readiness answer changes `readinessMatrix` → `coordinateColumns` → `progressSpecs` → `schemaColumns` (lines 297-301), which rebuilds every ColDef a second time.
failure_scenario: Edit one text cell on the Shared product sheet (GALE IT). Result: PATCH/bulk-save, then GET /studio/sheet (all rows replaced), then GET /readiness (family-wide, every coordinate and market). That is 3 requests and two full column-def rebuilds, so every visible cell renders at least twice. Budget: edit → saved ≤ 2 calls and ≤ 60 renders.
evidence: useMasterSheet.ts:166-179 (`quietRead.current = true; setNonce(n => n + 1)` in onSettled/onReconciled), :238-270 (the read replaces `sheet`). useMasterSheetAdapter.tsx:110-130 (refreshReadinessSoon → refreshReadiness() with no options), :297-301 and :363 (column memos keyed on `sheet` and `readinessMatrix`). contracts.tsx:1081-1085 (a non-coordinate refresh reads the family).
suggested_fix: Reuse the channel sheet's settle-in-place (savedCellPatch/rowSettle/FollowUpRead) for master cells whose answer determines the stored value. Key the master column model on column content, as the channel adapter does with columnsKey/viewCtx JSON. Feed progress columns their readiness through a ref, so a readiness answer refreshes cells instead of rebuilding ColDefs.

title: Channel sheet: most first fills, clears and warned values still reload the whole sheet, and that read replaces every grid row
description: `planSavedCellPatch` settles in place only for a narrow case. It falls back to a read when: the cell's mapping is not 'mapped' (an empty channel field with no rule is `status:'unmapped'`, resolve-batch.service.ts:379-395), the field is required (:137), the value is a listing-level eBay value that no family row supplies yet (:128), the edit is a clear (:123) or a reset (:111), or the answer carries any warning (:112). P1 now stores off-list and over-limit values with a warning, which adds to the read cases. The follow-up read (FollowUpRead → `refresh`) fetches the whole compact sheet. Contrary to the comment at useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:182-185, a fresh read gives every row a new grid object: `withRowIdentity` caches by the decoded server row object (rows.ts:173-183), and a new read always yields new objects. AG therefore re-renders every row.
failure_scenario: Completing a listing, the sheet's main use: on GALE eBay IT the operator types a first value into an empty 'Stagione' (required, strict) or into any empty unmapped item specific, or clears one. Result: bulk-save + GET /studio/sheet (compact, ~25–95 KB gz, plus ~200 ms server encode) + readiness = 3 calls, and all 105 rows re-render. During continuous editing the read is often dropped (an editor is open) and fetched again every 1.5 s until it applies.
evidence: savedCellPatch.ts:111-139 (read conditions). resolve-batch.service.ts:379-395 (an empty field with no rule is 'unmapped'). saveSettle.ts:74-90 (FollowUpRead). rows.ts:173-183 (WeakMap keyed by the server row). useChannelSheet.ts:148-163 (`refresh` → setResponse with new objects). The ground-truth file covers only 11 cases (9 patch, 2 read).
suggested_fix: Have bulk-save return the saved rows' recomputed cells (value, provenance, mapped status/errors, completeness) for the coordinate, and patch from that answer instead of reading the sheet. At least, derive the unmapped→override and required-fill cases from the column facts. On a read, reuse unchanged row objects by structural comparison (or a server row hash) so AG skips unchanged rows.

title: About 22 API calls on load (budget ≤ 15); 5 are formula batch reads that repeat formulas the sheet read already carries
description: Since P0 the sheet read seeds every cell's formula (`seedFromSheet`; studio-sheet.service.ts:1091-1110 and 1501-1507 read the same CellFormula rows with the same locale rule). Editors no longer wait for them. Yet `useCellFormulas` still sends one POST /pim/formulas/batch per alias × language × 250 rows on every load (and on every nonce/coordinate change), plus /pim/formulas/functions. Other load calls: a second /api/connections from AppNavRail (the frame already reads /connections?all=true), /sidebar/counts, three reference-label reads, layout + saved views, and SSE.
failure_scenario: Load of GALE eBay IT (5 aliases, 1 language): csrf, me, product, marketplaces/grouped, connections, destination, sheet, readiness, formulas/functions, 5× formulas/batch, categories/reference-labels, category-breadcrumbs, ebay/policies, layout, saved views, AppNavRail /connections, /sidebar/counts, listings/events SSE, about 22 in all. With locales=it,en,de there are 15 formula batch calls alone.
evidence: useCellFormulas.ts:155-160 (functions), :163-206 (batch requests = languages × aliases × ceil(rows/250), run 4 at a time). formulaReadiness.ts:34-47 (the seed makes rows known from the sheet). useReferenceNames.ts:70-80. useSheetColumns.ts:280-310 (layout). AppNavRail.tsx:41-44, 79-90.
suggested_fix: Skip the batch reads when the sheet read seeded every row for the requested languages (read them only for language columns the sheet did not carry, or on explicit Retry/reload). Cache /formulas/functions per session. Reuse the frame's connections read in the nav rail.

title: Reset of formula cells: one DELETE per cell with no concurrency limit, then two full sheet reads and all formula batches re-read
description: `reset` removes formulas with `Promise.all(formulas.map(removeFormula))`. That is one DELETE /pim/formulas/product/:id per cell, all at once, and there is no bulk removal route. Each DELETE goes through the formula queue, whose settle bumps the nonce, so every /formulas/batch read runs again. It also calls `onSettled` → `refresh()`, a full sheet GET that is discarded if the reset's own save is still pending. The reset's bulk-save then cannot be settled in place (`intent !== 'set'`), so FollowUpRead fetches the whole sheet again.
failure_scenario: Resetting ONE formula cell from the cell menu costs: DELETE, 5 × formulas/batch, GET /studio/sheet (often wasted), bulk-save, GET /studio/sheet, readiness, about 10 requests against a budget of 2. 'Reset column to inherited' over a 105-row formula column fires 105 concurrent DELETE requests (each a server transaction) before the one bulk-save.
evidence: useSheetControl.tsx:71-89. useCellFormulas.ts:146-151 (the queue settle → setNonce + onSettled) and :236-243 (pinOver = DELETE per cell). useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:237 (onSettled → refresh). savedCellPatch.ts:111 (a reset reads). formulaSaveQueue.ts:1-20.
suggested_fix: Add a bulk formula-removal endpoint, or fold formula removal into the reset's bulk-save units. Skip the formula queue's onSettled refresh when a writer operation follows. Update the formula state locally (`saveLocally(null)`) instead of re-reading every batch.

title: Bulk save is still 37–46 statements per row (budget ≤ 15); a 105-row paste is 3,857–4,485 round trips
description: The read memo roughly halved statements, but each unit still runs its own row writer. Per unit that means 12–15 Product SELECTs, 8–10 ChannelListing SELECTs, 3 ProductTranslation reads, and separate CellFormula, FieldLinkGroup and ProductCategory reads. It also writes one BulkOperation, one AuditLog, one ProductEvent and one ProductReadCache INSERT per row, plus SAVEPOINT/RELEASE, and runs `resolveBatch` twice for the information check (information-validation.ts:23,49; ~50–75 ms per unit on PGlite). Commit 95765c8ab says the 15-per-row budget was not reached.
failure_scenario: A 105-row eBay paste in production, one unit per row inside one Serializable transaction. At ~1.2 ms per round trip (the report's ~6 ms per statement was 5 round trips each), 4,000+ sequential statements take ~5 s before the readiness rebuild and the response. The plan's '105-row paste ≤ 3 s' is missed.
evidence: Audit test (deleted), eBay IT family, applyProductBulkSave. descriptionThemeId: 21 rows → 845 statements (40.2/row), 105 rows → 3,857 (36.7/row). Axis field: 21 rows → 957 (45.6/row), 105 rows → 4,485 (42.7/row). Top per-105-row counts: SELECT Product 1,588; SELECT ChannelListing 1,057; SELECT ProductTranslation 321; ProductCategory 212; INSERT BulkOperation/AuditLog/ProductEvent/ProductReadCache 105–106 each. The statement count grows linearly with rows (no quadratic statement count).
suggested_fix: Batch the per-row bookkeeping: one BulkOperation per sheet operation, and set-based audit, event and read-cache writes collected across units. Load product, listing and translation rows for all units once and pass them in. Run the information check once per operation over all changed products.

title: Render budget not met: the author measured 208 renders for a one-cell edit and 461 for a listing-level select (budget ≤ 60)
description: Each change in save status (pending → saving → saved) or in `lastSavedAt` re-renders the whole adapter and the entire ProductSheetSurface subtree. GridSheet is `memo`, but it receives a new `toolbar` element and footer on every render, so the memo never holds. SheetToolbar and the status and footer children are not memoized, and the model object and its inline handlers (e.g. `onCellKeyDown`) are rebuilt each render. A listing-level save also refreshes all 21 family rows.
failure_scenario: A one-cell text edit on AIRMESH eBay IT produced 208 component renders; one listing-level select produced 461 (commit 0e6e3f3e1 message). Both are 3.5–7.7× the plan's ≤ 60.
evidence: Commit 0e6e3f3e1: '9,374 -> 208 component renders … 13,016 -> 461 renders'. ProductSheetSurface.tsx:57-90 (new toolbar/footer JSX every render). GridSheet.tsx:55 (memo defeated). useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:388-406 (setLastSavedAt and status updates per settle).
suggested_fix: Memoize the toolbar and footer elements on their real inputs, split status (pending/saving/saved counts) into a small subscribed component instead of adapter state, and memoize SheetToolbar.

title: cells=compact costs more CPU than the transfer it saves (≈ 200 ms server encode + 75–100 ms browser decode per 6,300-cell read)
description: `encodeSheetCells` runs synchronously in the route after the sheet is built. It computes a per-key tally for every column (`baseOf`) and a patch per cell, using `JSON.stringify` comparisons in `same` and `identity`. `decodeSheetCells` deep-copies every cell on the browser's main thread. The API already gzips responses (index.ts:450), so on a normal link the byte saving is small next to the CPU.
failure_scenario: Synthetic 105 × 60 eBay sheet (953 B/cell raw). Plain: stringify 34 ms + gzip 48 ms server, 182 KB gz, parse 47 ms client. Compact: encode ~200 ms + stringify 9 + gzip 14 server, 66 KB gz, parse 10 + decode 74–100 ms client. Net: ~+175 ms of CPU for −116 KB, slower end-to-end above ~5 Mbps. The API event loop is also blocked ~200 ms on every sheet read, including every follow-up read after an edit.
evidence: Scratch benchmark (tsx, packages/shared/sheet-cell-wire.ts): {plainPerCell:953, compactPerCell:179, encodeMs:198–219, decodeMs:74–102, plainGzKB:182, compactGzKB:66, gzipPlainMs:48, gzipCompactMs:14, parsePlainMs:47, parseCompactMs:10}. CPU profile: baseOf, same, apply and patchOf dominate. Route: product-studio.routes.ts:582.
suggested_fix: Build the column base while the sheet service builds the cells (it knows the per-column constants), instead of rediscovering it by tallying. Or compare on precomputed per-column fingerprints rather than JSON.stringify per key. Decode lazily per visible row.

title: Recovery and read-back reads bypass the compact wire form
description: The load and quiet reads request `cells=compact`, but the writer's recovery reads still fetch the plain sheet: master `readBackBatch` and `readBack` (useMasterSheet.ts:138-160), and the channel `readScope` (useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:352-358, `channelScopeUrl(...)` with no `compactSheetUrl`). Two paths read the same sheet in different wire forms.
failure_scenario: After a save whose answer was lost (a flaky connection), the reconcile downloads the full plain sheet (~995 B/cell, 5× the compact size), on exactly the path where the connection is already unreliable, and repeats it while the writer keeps asking.
evidence: useMasterSheet.ts:138-160 (the URL has no `cells=compact`). useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:355. sheetUrls.ts:59 (`compactSheetUrl` exists).
suggested_fix: Wrap the recovery URLs in `compactSheetUrl` and decode with `decodeSheetCells` before `recoverSheetRow`.

title: Each reference-name read that lands after load rebuilds every column definition
description: Each lookup's `apply` sets `resolved`, and `nameReferenceColumns` returns new column objects with new `optionLabels`. On the channel sheet this changes `columnsKey` → `stableColumns` → `gridColumns` → `columnDefs` (useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:275-301), so AG re-creates every visible cell renderer. `nameReferenceColumns` also re-runs a regex over every option of every column whenever `sheet` changes.
failure_scenario: Opening GALE eBay IT: the reference-labels for category 177104, the category breadcrumbs and the eBay policies land separately after the first paint. That is 3 extra full column rebuilds and re-renders of every visible cell within the first seconds (more with several categories).
evidence: useReferenceNames.ts:44-47 (apply → setResolved per lookup), :115-120 (the columns memo). referenceLabels.ts:61-75. useChannelSheetAdapter.tsx:275-301.
suggested_fix: Give cell renderers and formatters the label maps through a stable ref or context and refresh only the affected columns (`refreshCells({columns})`), instead of changing ColDef inputs. Or wait for all name lookups before building the columns once.
